doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Basie's guitar chair, Claude Williams and Freddie Green
summary: Discussion of acoustic guitar in the Basie rhythm section and Freddie Green's steady beat.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Let me ask you something. I got to meet Claude “Fiddler” Williams. And apparently when Basie first came to New York, Claude was in the guitar chair.
Was he? I didn’t know about that.
No it couldn’t. No. Especially with Freddie, because he was so wonderful.
That sound of that — I mean I’m convinced in my own mind that the sound of that acoustic instrument just chomping —
Me too. I still think that. Do you still think that?
Yeah. I mean it just added that extra bit to the rhythm section.

It added a bit of something musical. You know, the chords, and the strings. I was thinking just the other day, Stanley was playing something very good, and I thought, what a pity they were so smart as to mix out the guitar. Because it was a wonderful rhythm instrument. And of course the guys used to say you know, Freddie wouldn’t let you — not Jo Jones, he was wonderful. But they used to say Freddie wouldn’t let you budge from the beat. Freddie was immovable from the beat, which was really quite wonderful. But anyway I’m sure we’re running out of time.
